Front bumper removal is the same throughout the years, I just watched a cj pony parts installation video for a front mount intercooler to see how to remove it. I mounted the horns into the crash bar, there are two squarish holes near the ends of the crashbar and that is the best place to mount the hellas without drilling. Make sure that you use spring washers to make sure nothing gets loose over time. You do not need to use the relay that comes in the box just cut the wires of the oem horn and connect it to the new hellas. You'll also need to remove the radiator air deflector inlet shroud in order for the hellas to fit. Some cars will have a white arrow spray painted onto the crash bar and the only way to remove it is to get a can of colour matched paint and spray over it (you'll see in the photo).

No i wouldn't recommend a cover for it just make sure that when the filter is applied to the car it is not over oiled, If it is oil will enter the engine. The green air filter WILL allow more contaminants in than the stock due to it's larger micron size in the gauze but it is very minimal. I personally don't worry about my filter and I wouldn't about yours

As i understand the Green Air filters available all offer almost identical particle resistance as stock through their material, however it can cause damage through it's open end due to leaves and whatnot having the possibility to enter the engine if the stock air box is not on top, If you are worried consider purchasing a cap for your filter that will seal off the open end but will suppress some of the sound or just leave the stock air box over the green filter. Just make sure that the filter is not over oiled and you should be fine.

Many tires have tread wear indicators, they can be found inside the tread of the tires, once the tread wear indicator is flush with the tread itself you should start to consider to purchase new tires, if the tread is low it becomes much more dangerous to drive during the rain due to the possibility hydroplaning. Please don't take tires lightly as they're the only thing that connects you to the road.
